relevance_note: Single-patient case report of an FLD patient carrying two LCAT variants: 'genetic analysis at age 13 revealed the presence of a frameshift mutation (NM_000229.2: c.576del ...) as well as a base-pair substitution (NM_000229.2: c.1034C>T ...)'.
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; JSON built with a short script in the scratch directory, every span checked verbatim against the paper by script. Scope: one patient (label 'patient'; 'the proband' is a role word) plus his father ('father of patient'), included because the paper gives individual-level facts (sudden cardiac death at 38) and annotates the c.576del allele as paternal; the mother is mentioned only via the 'maternal' allele annotation and gets no row. No variant row for either parent (carrier status is not stated as tested). Variants: protein descriptions are labelled 'mature protein' numbering in the paper. Inheritance taken from the '; paternal' / '; maternal' annotations next to each variant; the paper does not describe how parental origin was established. Zygosity left not reported: the paper never says 'compound heterozygous' (rule 8). Variant type for c.1034C>T left not reported: the paper calls it a 'base-pair substitution', not missense. Functional evidence (complete absence of plasma LCAT activity) is stated for the two variants together. Publications: cites_prior_report set true because facts about this patient's genotype/LCAT activity and transplants are cited to refs 4 (Miller 1995) and 5 (Ahmad 2016), without an explicit 'previously reported' sentence. Age at onset left not reported: LCAT deficiency was suspected at age 6 from a lipid profile (not a symptom), and the first corneal finding is given as age 12 in the Case report but 'around age 11' (whitish cast) in the Ophthalmic section; the Discussion also says proteinuria and corneal opacity were found at 'age 12 and 14, respectively', reversing the order given elsewhere (proteinuria first at 14, corneal opacity at 12). Feature-level onsets use the Case report/Renal sections. Age at diagnosis = genetic analysis at 13. Vital status left not reported (not stated). Glomerular sclerosis (FSGS) was found in biopsies of the transplanted kidney, not the native kidney; recorded observed with that detail. Renal function was within normal range at presentation (one year after second transplant); not recorded as an exclusion of CKD because CKD/ESRD is documented earlier. 'Elevated unesterified (free) cholesterol' left not reported: the paper says most cholesterol was unesterified (recorded as reduced cholesteryl ester fraction) and gives UC 37.2 mg/dL with reference N/A, but does not call UC elevated. Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease excluded from 'no cardiovascular events' plus unremarkable intima-media thickness. Table 1 lab values outside reference ranges (e.g. WBC 3.4) were not turned into features unless the text names the abnormality. Table 1 lists HDL-C 6 mg/dL with reference '>5', which looks inconsistent with the text's 'extremely low'; the text was used.
